songs.title: Plastic Angel
songs.style: Intimate electronic indie ballad, gently rolling 6/8, dotted-quarter pulse about 87 BPM, NOT straight 4/4. Keep the selected Kid Comet voice timbre, but use ONE natural mid-low lead, close and dry, conversational. NO octave doubling, pitch-shifted shadow voice, parallel-octave backing or stacked lead. Leave natural pauses. Cloudy electric piano, soft sub bass, brushed electronic clicks, tiny tremolo guitar and wavering analog pad. Warm tactile tape sound, fragile and unhurried. Harmonic guide: Ebmaj7–Gm7–Abmaj7, then Fm9–Bb13 turnaround; changing inversions, let phrases breathe over barlines. Solo lead throughout, no backing vocals even in chorus. Short instrumental coda, tender resolved ending. No pop power chorus, no EDM drop.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You gave me an angel
From a machine by the door
It cost you three quarters
And a trip back for more
One wing was bent backwards
You said that was fine
Nothing that stays with us
Comes out right every time

[Refrain]
Plastic angel
On a piece of string
You don't have to save me
You don't have to fix a thing
Stay beside the window
Let the morning through
Something almost weightless
Still can hold on to you

[Verse 2]
I moved to a new room
And I lost half my stuff
Your number stopped working
When the winter came up
But the hook by the window
Had a place you could hang
A little blue shadow
That the passing cars made

[Refrain]
Plastic angel
On a piece of string
You don't have to save me
You don't have to fix a thing
Stay beside the window
Let the morning through
Something almost weightless
Still can hold on to you

[Bridge]
I don't think you're watching
I don't think you know
But I leave the curtains open
When I go

[Final Refrain]
Plastic angel
On a piece of string
You don't have to save me
You don't have to fix a thing
Stay beside the window
Let the morning through
Something almost weightless
Still can hold on to you

[Instrumental Coda]

songs.title: Final Boss Feelings
songs.style: Dark electronic indie, syncopated broken beat, 111 BPM, 4/4 with offbeat accents, not four-on-the-floor. Keep the selected Kid Comet voice timbre, but use ONE natural mid-low lead, close and dry, conversational. NO octave doubling, pitch-shifted shadow voice, parallel-octave backing or stacked lead. Leave natural pauses. Tight dry drums, deep gritty synth-bass ostinato, clipped muted guitar, sparse analog stabs and short delay throws. More tension and forward motion than the relaxed songs. Harmonic guide F#m9–Dmaj7–Bm7–C#7; dominant turnaround with altered bass notes, stop recycling one pop loop. Verse strips to bass/drums, chorus gains percussion not vocal layers. Entirely single lead, brief spoken bridge, no octave doubles. Instrumental release and decisive ending. No EDM drop, no arena rock.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I can talk my way through anything
Till you ask me how I feel
Then I'm checking all the exits
Then I'm spinning on my heel
There's a joke I keep repeating
There's a drink I never finish
You can see me in the doorway
Trying not to be in it

[Chorus]
I know the move
I know the timing
Still I lose
When you get quiet
No big fight
No ceiling falling
Just your eyes
And all these final boss feelings

[Verse 2]
I've rehearsed it in the kitchen
With the water running hot
Had a speech for every ending
Except the one where you don't stop
You don't ask for an explanation
You just pull another chair
Now the thing that I've been fighting
Isn't even standing there

[Chorus]
I know the move
I know the timing
Still I lose
When you get quiet
No big fight
No ceiling falling
Just your eyes
And all these final boss feelings

[Spoken Bridge]
Could we leave the light on?
Could I stay a while?
I don't have an answer.
I'm just tired of getting out.

[Instrumental Break]

[Final Chorus]
I know the move
I know the timing
Still I lose
When you get quiet
No big fight
No ceiling falling
Just your eyes
And all these final boss feelings

[Outro]
Leave the light on
Let me stay a while

songs.title: Star Sticker Funeral
songs.style: Sparse reflective electronic indie, 73 BPM, loose half-time 4/4. Keep the selected Kid Comet voice timbre, but use ONE natural mid-low lead, close and dry, conversational. NO octave doubling, pitch-shifted shadow voice, parallel-octave backing or stacked lead. Leave natural pauses. Warm worn electric piano, round sub notes, brushed rim clicks, tiny room noises, long instrumental spaces. Harmonic guide Fmaj7–C/E–Dm9–Gsus2, suspended resolution and descending inner voice, open major colors rather than another minor dance loop. No constant drum pulse in first verse. ONE solo lead in all verses and choruses, absolutely no backing choir or octave unison; vocal almost speaking at moments. A small guitar response instead of a vocal double. Understated, human, quiet ending, no dramatic crescendo.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The stars came off in pieces
When I emptied out the drawer
Some silver on my fingers
Some glue that wouldn't go
I kept the little metal tin
That used to hold your change
And laid them in the bottom
With the tickets from that place

[Refrain]
Nothing much to bury
Nothing much to say
Just a bit of silver
From an ordinary day
Close the lid gently
Leave it on the shelf
Some things don't get bigger
When you keep them to yourself

[Verse 2]
I thought I'd feel much older
With the room so clean and bare
But I still knew where the posters
Left their corners in the paint
Your handwriting on a cassette
I'd forgotten how to play
I put it with the stickers
And I put the box away

[Instrumental Passage]

[Refrain]
Nothing much to bury
Nothing much to say
Just a bit of silver
From an ordinary day
Close the lid gently
Leave it on the shelf
Some things don't get bigger
When you keep them to yourself

[Bridge]
Not a proper ending
Not a great goodbye
I just stopped unpacking
And let the morning by

[Outro]
Close the lid gently
Leave it on the shelf

songs.title: Arcade Heaven
songs.style: Expansive warm electronic indie centerpiece, 104 BPM, gently driving 4/4. Keep the selected Kid Comet voice timbre, but use ONE natural mid-low lead, close and dry, conversational. NO octave doubling, pitch-shifted shadow voice, parallel-octave backing or stacked lead. Leave natural pauses. Deep round bass, dry pocket drums, slow analog chords, tremolo guitar and small crystalline synth answers. Verse harmony Dmaj9–A/C#–Bm9–E13; refrain opens to F#m7–C#m7–Dmaj7–Eadd9, bridge briefly shifts to Bm7–Dmaj7–A/E–E. Build depth through instruments, NOT doubled vocals. Solo lead through verses and first two refrains; ONLY the final two sung lines may have one quiet third-above harmony, never octave doubling. Airy, tangible, bittersweet release, not stadium pop, no EDM drop. Long warm instrumental landing.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
There was a light behind the cabinet
Where the wall had come away
I thought somebody left a window
In a room that wasn't there
You put the cartridge on the counter
With the label wearing thin
We had nothing left to put in
But the door let us in

[Refrain]
Arcade heaven
Wasn't high above the street
Just a room beyond the racket
With a place for us to breathe
No one waiting for an answer
No one telling us to leave
Arcade heaven
Leave a little light for me

[Verse 2]
There were games we never finished
There were names we couldn't read
There were summers in the carpet
There were clouds beneath our feet
You were laughing at the doorway
Like you'd known it all along
We'd been looking for a way out
And we'd found a way back home

[Refrain]
Arcade heaven
Wasn't high above the street
Just a room beyond the racket
With a place for us to breathe
No one waiting for an answer
No one telling us to leave
Arcade heaven
Leave a little light for me

[Bridge]
I don't need to stay forever
I don't need the time to stop
Let me take this small thing with me
When the morning opens up

[Final Refrain]
Arcade heaven
Wasn't high above the street
Just a room beyond the racket
With a place for us to breathe
No one waiting for an answer
No one telling us to leave

[Final two lines, quiet harmony in thirds only]
Arcade heaven
Leave a little light for me

[Instrumental Outro]

songs.title: Insert Coin to Dream
songs.style: INSTRUMENTAL ONLY, no singing, humming, vocal chops or spoken words. Short electronic indie album opening, about 65-85 seconds, 84 BPM loose 4/4. Coin-slot click becomes soft rim percussion, warm sub bass, wavering analog synth, sparse electric piano and one small plucked square-wave motif. Dmaj9–Bm11–Gmaj7–Aadd9, suspended colorful voicings, open space. Start with room tone and a click, let a lazy groove arrive halfway, then a short resolved tail. Tactile tape hiss, curious and intimate, not cinematic bombast, no EDM build. Same warm dusty electronic world as Kid Comet, no full chiptune arrangement.

songs.title: Continue?
songs.style: INSTRUMENTAL ONLY, no vocals, humming, choir, speech or vocal samples. Compact electronic indie interlude, 60-90 seconds. 101 BPM in a subtle flowing 5/4 meter grouped 3+2, a gently lopsided loop that feels suspended rather than frantic. Muted analog bass, soft dry broken percussion, slow electric-piano figures and tiny pulse-wave countdown answers. Cm9–Abmaj7–Fm9–G7, voice-led voicings, brief dominant tension; leave an extra beat of air. Tape warmth and CRT-like soft high texture. One small melodic event in the middle, clean ending, no big drop, no generic soundtrack swell.

songs.title: Sunrise After Game Over
songs.style: INSTRUMENTAL ONLY, no lead vocals, humming, choir or vocal samples. Warm electronic indie album closing piece, about 90-120 seconds, 69 BPM gentle 3/4 waltz. Simple unhurried electric-piano melody, soft analog bass and airy synth pad, barely-there brushed electronic percussion, small clean tremolo-guitar reply. Gmaj9–Em7–Am9–D13 with changing inversions, melodic rising sixth recalling a summer memory. Start nearly bare, open slightly in the middle, end with a long natural warm chord decay. Hopeful morning, tactile tape character, quieter than the title song. No bombastic crescendo or EDM drop.
